diagnosis.opening: Desktop rail hover, focus, or click opens transiently; touch uses stable open behavior. Pin toggles transient/pinned. Drawer accessibility state is aria-hidden=false whenever state is not peek.
diagnosis.closing: Desktop transient state closes after a 400 ms pointer-out delay unless focus remains inside; Escape and the close action close explicitly. Route, mode, task, or narrow-layout changes reset state.
diagnosis.semanticOpenState: data-drawer-state plus rail aria-expanded; drawer aria-hidden is derived from state !== peek.

animation.desktop: transform and visibility transition, 190 ms ease/step timing
animation.narrow: static in-flow layout with no transition

observations: All eleven target identities passed with 1 worker and zero retries; the same representative test also passed alone.
With 2 workers, 9/11 passed and two Oblique Architecture cases timed out while waiting for task actions; there were no retries.

With 4 workers and no instrumentation, 4/11 passed and 7 failed; five failures were completed-position transform assertions showing nonzero translateX while the drawer was semantically open, and two were content/text assertions.

In the controlled diagnostic traces, requestedOpen became true and drawerState became transient while the drawer remained mounted, aria-hidden=false, and the document visible. The sampled transform initially remained at -288 px.

In one guided heavy-load trace, first observed transitionrun occurred 1603.1 ms after the open-state mutation; a later sampled transitionrun occurred 592.1 ms after mutation with lightweight peers. Both target tests eventually reached transform zero and passed. Each profile was run once.

The controlled trace sampled long animation-frame gaps (about 0.7–0.9 s under the heavy profile and about 0.29 s under the light profile in the recorded interval). The instrumentation was diagnostic-only and the clean four-worker cohort report is the outcome evidence.
The six existing overlay regressions passed, covering pointer-out, keyboard focus, internal scrolling, responsive flow, and expanded Ground Glass layout.

The current four-worker run also produced a missing lesson-stage text assertion in Oblique Architecture; this differs from its historical transform signature and the M7K Oblique Tabletop content failure remains separate.

hypotheses.evidence: The sampled failures had requestedOpen=true, transient state, aria-hidden=false, and a mounted drawer; sampled controlled traces did not show a superseding close. This does not rule out races in unobserved runs.

Clean four-worker failures retained intermediate translateX while semantically open; controlled traces showed delayed frames/transition start under load. One attempt per controlled profile is insufficient to establish a universal cause.
No unexpected close was observed in controlled samples. The existing pointer-out regression passed, but this does not eliminate every pointer race.

Three WebGL-heavy peers and three lightweight peers both allowed the guided target to pass; one paired timing sample was slower with heavy peers. This is suggestive only and does not establish renderer contention as a sole cause.
The Oblique Tabletop missing Step 1 content and the current Oblique Architecture stage text failure are content assertions; evidence does not connect them to CSS transform scheduling.

diagnosis.supportedCause: No single shared root cause is established. Browser frame/transition scheduling pressure is the best-supported contributor to the transform failures; the content failures remain separate and unresolved.
rejectedCauses: No demonstrated drawer close-state mutation during the sampled transform failures.
No demonstrated responsive breakpoint change in the desktop transform failures.
diagnosis.confidence: moderate for concurrency-sensitive transition scheduling as a contributor; low for a single shared root cause or renderer-specific causality
limitations: One attempt per worker configuration and controlled profile.
The primary four-worker capture was uninstrumented; diagnostic traces use a temporary test-only observer and are not a clean outcome run.
No full 278-test suite, native GPU capture, or matched product-fix run was performed.

remediation.decision: Keep all eleven assertions and the existing renderer scheduling policy. The evidence establishes sensitivity but not a specific application defect or a safe synchronization fix.
